summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of polymyositis, morbid obesity, and prior pulmonary emboli was admitted for progressive shortness of breath and leg swelling. She had gained 19 pounds in a week despite increased Lasix, following a recent steroid dose reduction and Rituximab infusion. Imaging ruled out pulmonary embolism but showed mild pulmonary congestion, leading to a diagnosis of acute on chronic diastolic heart failure exacerbated by steroid-induced fluid retention. She received IV furosemide with significant improvement in symptoms and fluid balance. Her polymyositis remained stable with trending-down CK and troponin. Warfarin was adjusted to maintain therapeutic INR, and metformin was restarted at discharge. She was discharged on increased furosemide, continued steroid taper, and outpatient follow-up with instructions for daily weight monitoring and low-sodium diet.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
